sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity (June 2025): no specific law criminalising LGBT+ identity as such, but at least 139 individuals affected by anti-LGBT+ laws including 'gay propaganda' convictions, detentions and 'extremism' prosecutions; no SOGI discrimination legislation; the note's central distinction is that general state risk is not established across the country except in the North Caucasus, and it notes there is no reliable data on the size or distribution of the LGBT+ population.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (blocked by a security service); the underlying source is the US State Department's country travel advisory, which advises against all travel regardless of any personal characteristic due to wrongful-detention and arbitrary-law-enforcement risk.

sources.title: Russia: Rising Toll of LGBT ‘Extremism’ Designation | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): courts issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in or display of symbols of the alleged 'International LGBT Movement'; repeated display of a banned symbol carries up to four years' imprisonment; cases include forced labour after posting a rainbow flag on social media, and administrative sentences that prompted users to delete accounts out of fear of prosecution.
